I’m going to say something, and this time it’s personal.

When Bitcoin was trading around $87K, I was one of the few who trusted their medium- to long-term analysis and refused to fall for the bounce.

And you know what I received?

Insults. Mockery. Disrespect.

An unbelievable amount of hate simply because I refused to follow the crowd.

But here’s what I find truly disappointing.

When my analysis turns out to be right, the support is nowhere near as loud as the hate was.

Think about that for a moment.

I’ve been in this space for years. Through multiple cycles, countless narratives, and endless waves of market euphoria and fear.

And whether you like me or not, I’ve remained one of the few accounts consistently willing to make bold calls and stand behind them.

I don’t expect everyone to agree with me. But there’s a difference between disagreeing with someone and disrespecting them.

I’ll leave you with something to reflect on:

People are incredibly loud when they think you’re wrong, but strangely silent when you prove them wrong.

And despite everything, I’m still here.

Still sharing my analysis. Still trusting my convictions.

You don’t have to like me. But you can’t erase the track record just because it hurts your ego.

quote.text:
$BTC Open Interest (in BTC) is back at the highest level we've seen since 2021-2023. 

Every time we hit this area during the past year, we saw a flush of open interest soon after. Usually this was due some sort of squeeze in the market which made the open interest top out.

Keep in mind, this says nothing about which direction that squeeze should be in. But in the majority of the other examples on the chart it did cause a reversal in the market instead of further continuation.

This makes sense as positions tend to build up during a trend. Then when that trend reverses you see those positions cover to take profit or get squeezed out. The other side of the trade generally already got washed out multiple times before.

tweets.text:
You can be right about direction and still get liquidated before the move happens

That's the problem “Futures without liquidation” is trying to solve

So, let's talk about how it works:

CASE STUDY

Let's say you open a BTC long because you are expecting a pump

> Traditional futures: Price drops, liquidates you, and finally goes up without you

> Futures without liquidation: Price drops, your position loses value, but the drop doesn't force a liquidation

When you open a trade, you choose an expiry date. You can close earlier or let it settle at expiry.

That means:

If BTC recovers while the contract is still open, your position can recover value too
But, if your contract expires on Friday, a recovery on Saturday is too late.

HOW IT WORKS

The product uses options underneath to give exposure similar to futures

That's why it has an expiry date and no margin liquidation level

You are paying for that exposure over a specific period of time

Staying longer means opening a new contract and paying for more time

COSTS

Costs include:

> 0.01% of position value when opening and closing
> The spread
> Funding to expiration (shown before entry)

So 0.01% isn't the total cost of the trade.

MY OPINION

I think this could be useful for the traders who have conviction about a move, but expect a lot of volatility along the way

You can still lose money, no liquidation doesn't mean no losses

A man always needs a plan

That said, it's an interesting tool. I will keep exploring it and sharing my experience.

Would you use it for your trades?

overheard from friends talking about AI in China, and it’s very alarming

- AI short films went massive in China market because of how good the video models are now

- the first wave of people who mastered using AI to generate short films and comics made quite some money because they could produce a lot more content than traditional workflows

- but within just a few months, everybody and their mom could make equally good short films because all the expertise could be written in a markdown file

- when everyone’s more productive, no one actually has an advantage and it’s a race to the bottom. very quickly it became impossible to make money, and everyone’s busier than they were without AI

- the only one making money now is companies like bytedance who owns user demand and distribution. they sell ads to creators who pay to get traffic, and eventually ad spend became 80% of those creators’ operating expense, while AI tokens is less than 5%

so what are the problems here? 

1. there’s no moat if you are creating anything with AI

if a human is really good at something, and it’s hard to find more humans who can do the same, they can leverage the scarcity of their skill to get paid very well

but if AI is good at something, it will be infinitely replicated, so there’s no scarcity hence you can’t really expect a sustainable business by creating anything with AI

2. more creators created more content people actually liked. that’s a good thing

but the economical benefit of that all got absorbed by the distribution platforms

there’s a famous chinese poem 遍身罗绮者，不是养蚕人 - it basically says people who dress well aren’t the people making dresses. that’s exactly what’s happening here

if our society doesn’t figure out a better way to distribute wealth, AI will help billionaires become trillionaires while average people become more exhausted than ever
